comment: Checks qa-flow can run against a USER'S repo. Format documented in rails-flow/checks.json.
Deliberately NOT listed: rendered_conformance and anything else needing a browser. Those need
Playwright, which is the user's dependency and not installable from here -- and a check that
silently skips for a missing dependency is worse than no check. They belong in the browser
pass the agent drives, not in a gate that must be honest without one.
EVIDENCE LIVES IN TWO DIRECTORIES, and every path here must name the one that applies (#423).
qa/manual-tests/ is the browser workspace -- the crawl's JSON and the per-run summary/runtime
CSVs. qa/reports/ is where the structured report artefacts land: the a11y, keyboard, forms,
emulation and perf page CSVs, the deduped findings CSV, the route table, and one directory per
manifested run. A path aimed at the wrong one is NOT a failure -- project_gates.py reports an
absent path as not-applicable -- so it is a permanent silent skip. scripts/check_manifest_paths.py
reconciles every path below against the paths this plugin's own scripts and commands name.

checks.why: Evidence whose pages were never validated as the pages under test proves nothing.
The a11y, keyboard, forms, emulation, perf and findings profiles write to qa/reports/, so the glob above reaches none of them.
A long browser run must leave reviewable evidence, not a directory of orphans.
Which routes QA has never touched -- reported, so completeness is never implied.
A route that returns 200 while rendering an error page passes every status check.
A control can be named, focusable and correctly marked up, and still do nothing when clicked.
A link to a route nobody listed is never crawled, and a 404 sub-resource is not a failed request.
A screen with no baseline has never been reviewed; a changed one may be a regression.
